role_in_parent: Shows that valley sets are independent sets in the path {1,...,n}, which is the structural input for the weighted independent-set bound.
statement_nl: Let n be an integer with n at least 2, and let s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) be a sign sequence with each s_i equal to plus 1 or minus 1. Define the valley set V(s) subset of {1,...,n} by: 1 belongs to V(s) exactly when s_1 = plus 1; n belongs to V(s) exactly when s_{n-1} = minus 1; and for 2 <= j <= n-1, j belongs to V(s) exactly when s_{j-1} = minus 1 and s_j = plus 1. Then no two consecutive integers belong to V(s). Moreover, if a=(a_1,...,a_n) is a permutation of {1,...,n} such that s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0 for every i=1,...,n-1, and if a_j = 1, then j belongs to V(s).

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2
s has exactly n minus 1 entries
Each entry s_i is either plus 1 or minus 1
V(s) contains only integers from 1 through n
a is a permutation of 1 through n, so it is a rearrangement of those integers with no repeats
The inequality s_i times the difference a_{i+1} minus a_i is required for every i from 1 through n minus 1
The clause a_j equals 1 only makes sense for indices j from 1 through n
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Given any integer n at least 2 and any sign sequence s of length n minus 1 with entries plus 1 or minus 1, the valley set V(s) has no adjacent integers. Also, for any permutation a of 1 through n that strictly increases or decreases according to the signs s_i between consecutive entries, whenever the value 1 appears at position j in a, that position j must lie in V(s).
quantifier_order: For all integers n with n at least 2
For all sign sequences s of length n minus 1 with each entry equal to plus 1 or minus 1
Define V(s) by the stated endpoint and interior rules
Then no two consecutive integers are both in V(s)
For all permutations a of 1 through n such that for every i from 1 to n minus 1, s_i times the difference a_{i+1} minus a_i is positive
For all indices j from 1 to n, if a_j equals 1 then j is in V(s)

Membership in V(s) is determined solely by s and the index j, not by a
